text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Legislation is being prepared to regulate offshore banking, which is expected to attract much-needed international finance to Namibia after implementation early next year.
- Two people have been killed by explosives left over from Namibia's liberation war, bringing the total number of deaths in such incidents this year to six.
- The government has instructed a cabinet committee to investigate the ownership structures of the Meatco abattoir.
- The United Democratic Front accused President Sam Nujoma of double standards in handling demonstrations.
- A 1991 plan for nationalisation of meat-processing company Meatco is being pursued again with a special cabinet committee appointed to look into the company's ownership structures.

- An Angolan diplomat has criticised a recent decision to deport 350 illegal immigrants, among them 75 Angolans. He said they were refugees who had fled the UNITA-controlled Cuando-Cubango province to Namibia, for fear of being conscripted by former rebel movement.
